author: Yffe
content:
Failing test (pinned, #[ignore]d) at forge/tests/divergence_mutual_recursion.rs::divergence_mutual_recursion_is_rejected_not_crashed.

DIVERGENCE: .design/basis/10-recursion-tuples.md REQ-6 (+ Architecture + the REQ-2 validator doc-comment) promise a mutually-recursive pair without a dec chain 'reaches Verus and is rejected there (no false L3, no crash)'. forge::check::classify_verus_outcome (forge/src/check.rs) maps Verus's termination rejection 'recursive function must have a decreases clause' (encountered-vir-error: true) to ForgeError::VerusOutput — an ENVIRONMENT abort: exit 2, EMPTY --json stdout, NO certificate. That is a crash in the design's sense (no verdict produced).

CONTRAST (authority, R-CHAR-3): the SAME termination-failure class on a SINGLE self-recursive fn whose dec does not decrease yields a clean parseable L0 cert (exit 0) — recursion_conformance.rs::nondecreasing_recursion_is_l0, REQ-4/AC-2. The mutual case must likewise produce a non-L3 certificate verdict (reject/L0), not an uninterpretable VIR abort.

Probe (real verus 0.2026.05.24):
  fn a(n) { b(n-1) } / fn b(n) { a(n-1) }  no dec, fx pure
  -> forge check --json: exit 2, stdout empty, stderr 'could not interpret verus output: verus reported an internal (VIR) error; ... recursive function must have a decreases clause'

NON-laundering holds (not L3) — the divergence is the 'no crash' clause + the §5.1/R-SPEC-3 'certificate is the deliverable' contract.
